chung.Description:
This course explores the effect of cultural differences on organisational behaviour and negotiation in the global context. It exposes students to issues and problems that inevitably arise in international business when managers have to deal with culturally determined differences in values, attitudes and behaviours.

The course assists students in developing cross-cultural communication competence and management and negotiation skills to successfully solve problems and capitalise on opportunities in a multicultural environment.

clo: Describe cultural dimensions based on cultural frameworks and apply them to global business settings.
Develop cultural intelligence to interact and manage people from different cultures.
Developing capability to competently apply course concepts in cross- cultural situations that require responses at the individual, managerial and organisational levels.

Identify the major dimensions of culture relevant to work settings and discuss their effect on behavior in an international environment. Describe negotiation styles in different cultures; adjust negotiation tactics to cultural differences.
Explain the motivation, leadership and HR selection across cultures.
Develop cultural sensitivity needed to succeed in any kind of cross-cultural interactions.
Differentiate the different types of negotiation approaches (integrative, distributive negotiations).
Describe the strategies and actions taken on different stages of negotiations; appreciate and explain the importance of pre-; during and post-negotiation phases.
List the roles and functions in negotiation teams; demonstrate the skills of organizing and managing negotiation teams.
Identify different negotiation scenarios, then formulate and apply the instruments of negotiation strategy and tactics.
